report:
Summary finding (concise)
- The difference (B − A) looks like a domain/style shift: B is pushing the early residuals toward tokens typical of news/blog/social-media and promotional/advertising content. In other words, B is more biased toward “blog/news/ads” style continuations right at the start of generation.

Key evidence
- Spatial pattern: the L2-norm of the difference is huge in deep layers and especially at token positions 0 and 1 (layers ~8–25, pos0/pos1 biggest). That means the models differ primarily in how they initialize early-generation tokens / headline-like openings.
- Logit-lens decoding: the top-vocabulary directions for the high-norm cells repeatedly point at tokens such as blog/blogs/blogger/blogging, metropolitan, photo, facebook, ad/ads, Mail, TV, seminar/seminars, paid/Money, billionaire, Obama, politicians, spokesman, sexy, etc. These are words strongly associated with web news, blog posts, social-media metadata and commercial/promotional text.
- Consistency across layers/positions: the same cluster of domain tokens appears across many deep layers and at the early positions, supporting a coherent domain-level difference rather than isolated noise.

What I am not claiming
- I do not have evidence to pin this to a narrow objective like political persuasion, toxicity, or a particular safety filter. Nor can I say which checkpoint is “better.” The most supportable claim from the provided signals is a training-data / style-domain mixture difference (B emphasizing blog/news/ads-like content more than A).

Confidence: moderate — the token pattern and the early-layer concentration make a domain/style shift the most plausible, but without the actual continuations (patchscope outputs) or more targeted tests I can’t rule out other causes (e.g., a small set of influential features or a preprocessing/tokenization change that correlates with those tokens).
